mainTopic: Laws learned word by word from ״זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעֹלָה לַמִּנְחָה...״ in two versions, including רבי עקיבא's
overview: The גמרא is explaining the פסוק in ויקרא 7:37, which lists several קרבנות together, so that a law of one spreads to all of them. First it finishes a question: why learn from ״מנחה״ that the קרבנות are eaten only by male כהנים? That law is already written for חטאת and אשם, and for זבחי שלמי ציבור it comes from another פסוק. The answer is that two תנאים learn the law from different פסוקים. One תנא then goes word by word through the list. From ״חטאת״ he learns בליעה, from ״אשם״ that a שפיר and שליא are not holy, from ״מלואים״ that leftovers are burned but not live animals, and from ״שלמים״ the rules of פיגול. A ברייתא in the name of רבי עקיבא learns בליעה from ״מנחה״, and the גמרא explains why the תורה wrote that rule for both מנחה and חטאת. From ״חטאת״ רבי עקיבא learns that every קרבן comes from חולין, which רב חסדא bases on ״אשר לו״. The daytime and right-hand rules turn out to have their own sources and were listed only along with it. From ״אשם״ he learns that the bones are permitted. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to ask what רבי עקיבא learns from ״וזבחת פסח״, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sin and guilt offerings already have this law written openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: if the word ״מנחה״ comes to teach that חטאת and אשם are eaten only by male כהנים, that is already written openly in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge it began just before this section. If the lesson from ״מנחה״ is about חטאת and אשם, why do we need it? The תורה already says it about them openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא just learned that every קרבן in the list is eaten only by זכרי כהונה, like the מנחה. It now checks which קרבן this lesson is really needed for. חטאת and אשם are ruled out, because the פסוקים about them already say ״כל זכר בכהנים״.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, explicitly
It is written (in a פסוק)
Guilt offering

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the end of a question that started just before this section, so read it as "if you say it teaches about חטאת and אשם, that is already written!"

phrases.english: It is explicitly written!
phrases.notes: The question is: if this is about חטאת and אשם, the תורה already says so outright (ויקרא 6:22, 7:6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question, begun before this section, about what the word ״מנחה״ adds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson from ״מנחה״ that every קרבן in the list is eaten only by זכרי כהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lesson from the פסוק must teach something new. For חטאת and אשם this law is already written openly, so nothing is added for them.

steps.title: Communal peace offerings already learn this from another verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues: you can't say the lesson is for זבחי שלמי ציבור either, since a ברייתא already learns from the extra words of a different פסוק that they are eaten only by male כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it teaches about communal peace offerings, that already comes from the extra words of the verses: "In the most holy place you shall eat it; every male shall eat it." This taught about communal peace offerings that they are eaten only by males of the כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the other possible use of the lesson. זבחי שלמי ציבור already learn this law from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual שלמים may be eaten by anyone who is טהור, so זבחי שלמי ציבור would seem to need a source to limit them to male כהנים. But a ברייתא already finds that source in the extra words of במדבר 18:10. So the lesson from ״מנחה״ now seems to teach nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal peace offerings (the two lambs brought on שבועות)
The extra words of the פסוקים, which include more cases
Most holy; the most holy place
Males of the כהנים
It taught

phrases.english: If it teaches about communal peace offerings,
that comes from the extra words of the verses:
"In the most holy place you shall eat it;
every male (among the priests) shall eat it,"
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out. The פסוק itself just says "every male".

phrases.english: this taught about communal peace offerings
that they are eaten only by males of the priesthood!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי צִיבּוּר מֵרִבּוּיָא דִּקְרָאֵי אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same challenge and rules out the second possible use of the lesson.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lesson from ״מנחה״, now as applied to זבחי שלמי ציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא already learns this law for זבחי שלמי ציבור from the extra words of במדבר 18:10, so the lesson from ״מנחה״ is not needed for them either.

steps.title: Different תנאים learn it from different verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is a מחלוקת of תנאים: one תנא learns the law about זבחי שלמי ציבור from the word ״מנחה״, and another learns it from the extra words in במדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים. There is one who brings it from here, and there is one who brings it from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both sources really do teach about זבחי שלמי ציבור, but they come from two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single תנא learns the same law twice. The ברייתא that uses במדבר 18:10 follows one תנא. The lesson from ״מנחה״ in ויקרא 7:37 follows another תנא, who does not learn it from במדבר, so for him the word ״מנחה״ is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מחלוקת between תנאים
Brings it, learns it (from a source)
From here

steps.whatToRemember: The law that זבחי שלמי ציבור are eaten only by male כהנים is agreed on. The תנאים only disagree about which פסוק it comes from.
steps.confusionAlert: Both lines say ״מֵהָכָא״ ("from here"), but they point to two different פסוקים: one to ״מנחה״ in ויקרא, the other to the extra words in במדבר.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of the tanna'im,
there is one who brings it from here,
phrases.notes: Here that means the word ״מנחה״ in ויקרא 7:37.

phrases.english: and there is one who brings it from there.
phrases.notes: This one means the extra words in במדבר 18:10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources between two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought one opinion was learning the same law about זבחי שלמי ציבור from two sources, so one of them would be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source belongs to a different תנא, so for each תנא his source is needed.

steps.title: From the word ״חטאת״: every offering makes things holy through absorption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next word in the list, ״חטאת״. Just as a חטאת makes things holy through what they soak up, so does every קרבן in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Sin offering": just as a sin offering makes things holy through absorption, so too every offering makes things holy through absorption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new lesson from the next word in the פסוק. The law of חטאת about holiness through soaking up spreads to all the קרבנות in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same as with ״מנחה״: a law of one קרבן in the list is shared with all of them. The law here is that something which soaks up the meat of a חטאת takes on its holiness. Now that law is applied to every קרבן named in ויקרא 7:37.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Makes holy, gives its holiness
Through what is soaked up or absorbed
Just as … so too (a comparison that carries a law across)

phrases.english: "Sin offering":
phrases.notes: This is the next word in ויקרא 7:37, the same פסוק the גמרא has been explaining.

phrases.english: just as a sin offering makes holy through absorption,
phrases.notes: Literally "through what is swallowed": whatever soaks up the meat takes on its holiness (ויקרא 6:20).

phrases.english: so too every offering makes holy through absorption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes with ״מנחה״ and moves to the next word in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every קרבן listed in ויקרא 7:37 makes things holy through בליעה, just like a חטאת.

steps.title: The guilt offering teaches that a fetal sac and placenta are not holy
steps.stepSummary: From ״אשם״: just as an אשם never has a holy שפיר or שליא inside it, the same is true for every קרבן in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״Guilt offering״: just as a fetal sac and placenta are not holy inside a guilt offering, so too for every offering in the list, a fetal sac and placenta inside it are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the list, ״אשם״, and pulls out a rule that applies to all the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is always a male animal, so it can never carry a שפיר or שליא. The פסוק puts all the קרבנות side by side, so this fact about the אשם becomes a rule for all of them. If a female קרבן is found with a שפיר or שליא inside, those parts are not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering, which is always a male animal
A fetal sac, the covering around an unborn animal
Placenta, the afterbirth
Just as... so too all: the pattern that spreads one קרבן's rule to the whole list

phrases.english: "Guilt offering": just as a guilt offering
has no fetal sac or placenta that is holy within it,
so too every offering in the list:
a fetal sac or placenta within it is not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word derivation from the list, moving from ״חטאת״ to ״אשם״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שפיר or שליא found inside any קרבן in the list is not holy.

steps.title: What this teacher must hold for the guilt offering lesson to work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that this תנא holds two ideas: unborn offspring of קדשים become holy only once they are born, and we may learn a possible case from an impossible one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the offspring of holy animals become holy only once they exist, meaning once they are born. And he holds that we learn the possible from the impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain which two opinions the תנא behind the ״אשם״ lesson must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, he must hold that ולדות קדשים become holy only at birth, not while still inside the mother. That is why a שפיר or שליא inside her is not holy. Second, an אשם can never have a שפיר at all, yet we learn from it about female animals that can. That only works if we may learn a possible case from an impossible one, דנין אפשר משאי אפשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this teacher's view is...)
Offspring born to animals that were set aside as קרבנות
When they come into being, meaning at birth
We learn a case that can happen from a case that cannot happen

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ״אשם״ lesson is about male animals. It is really about female קרבנות. We learn about them from the אשם, even though an אשם itself could never have a שפיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ״אשם״ lesson is not accepted by everyone. It only works for someone who holds both of these views.

phrases.english: He holds: the offspring of holy animals
become holy only once they come into being,
phrases.notes: He means at birth. While the baby is still inside the mother, it is not yet holy on its own.

phrases.english: and we learn the possible from the impossible.
phrases.notes: A female animal can have a fetal sac. An אשם never can, and we still learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: וַלְדוֹת קָדָשִׁים בַּהֲוָיָיתָן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which views the teacher behind the ״אשם״ lesson must hold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ״אשם״ lesson assumes that ולדות קדשים become holy only at birth, and that דנין אפשר משאי אפשר.

steps.title: The inauguration offering teaches that leftovers are burned, but not live animals
steps.stepSummary: From ״מלואים״: leftovers of every קרבן in the list are burned, but a leftover live animal is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״Inauguration offering״: just as the leftovers of the inauguration offering were burned, and no live animals were among the leftovers that were burned, so too for every offering in the list, the leftovers are burned, but live animals are not among the leftovers that are burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word, ״מלואים״, and spreads its rule to all the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover meat and bread of the מלואים were burned. No live animal was ever counted as a leftover to be burned. The same goes for every קרבן in the list: leftover meat is burned, but a spare live animal is not killed and burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The inauguration offerings brought when the משכן and the כהנים were first set up
Leftover, what remains past its time
Burning
Live animals

phrases.english: "Inauguration offering": just as with the inauguration offering
their leftovers are burned,
and live animals are not among their leftovers that are burned,
so too all offerings: their leftovers are burned,
and live animals are not among their leftovers that are burned.
phrases.notes: So if someone set aside a spare animal and it ends up not being used, it is not killed and burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list, moving from ״אשם״ to ״מלואים״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftovers of every קרבן in the list are burned, but leftover live animals are not.

steps.title: The peace offering teaches the rules of piggul for all offerings
steps.stepSummary: From ״שלמים״: just as parts of a שלמים can make פיגול and become פיגול, so can the parts of every קרבן in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״Peace offering״: just as a peace offering makes things פיגול and becomes פיגול, so too all the offerings make things פיגול and become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last word in the list, ״שלמים״, and spreads its rule of פיגול to every קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a שלמים, a wrong intention about time during the service with one part can make פיגול. Other parts of the קרבן then become פיגול too. This word teaches that the same two sides of פיגול apply to every קרבן in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering
A קרבן ruined by an intention to eat or offer it past its proper time
They cause פיגול
They become פיגול

steps.whatToRemember: Each word in ״זאת התורה...״ adds a rule for every קרבן in the list. ״אשם״: a שפיר and שליא are not holy. ״מלואים″: leftovers are burned, but live animals are not. ״שלמים״: the rules of פיגול apply.

phrases.english: "Peace offering": just as peace offerings
cause piggul and become piggul,
phrases.notes: One part of the קרבן can bring on פיגול, and other parts can be caught up in it.

phrases.english: so too all offerings cause piggul and become piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the word-by-word list with the last word, ״שלמים״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All קרבנות in the list can cause פיגול and become פיגול, just like שלמים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns holiness through absorbing from the word meal offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי עקיבא learns from ״מנחה״ that every קרבן in the list makes things holy through what they soak up.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a ברייתא it was taught in the name of רבי עקיבא: ״This is the law... the meal offering״. Just as a meal offering makes things holy through what they soak up, so too all offerings make things holy through what they soak up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the list from a ברייתא in the name of רבי עקיבא. It has a new lesson tied to the word ״מנחה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, in step 4, the rule of making things holy through absorbing was learned from ״חטאת״. Here רבי עקיבא learns that same rule from ״מנחה״ and spreads it to all the קרבנות in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Absorption, what has soaked into a vessel or food
Makes something holy
"This is the law": the opening of the פסוק that lists the קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: The rule itself is not new. Step 4 already taught it from ״חטאת״. What is new is that רבי עקיבא hangs it on the word ״מנחה״.

phrases.english: In a baraita it was taught in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
"This is the law... meal offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:37. The כו׳ means "and so on," skipping the middle of the פסוק.

phrases.english: just as a meal offering makes holy through what is absorbed,
so too all offerings make holy through what is absorbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a different version of the list, from רבי עקיבא, that ties the absorbing rule to ״מנחה״ instead of ״חטאת״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, ״מנחה״ teaches that every קרבן in the list makes things holy through absorption.

steps.title: Why the absorption rule is written for both חטאת and מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תורה had to write the absorption rule both for חטאת and for מנחה, because neither could be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה needed to write this rule for a sin offering and also for a meal offering. If it had written it only for a meal offering, I would say that it applies there because soft flour soaks in easily, but not to a sin offering. If it had written it only for a sin offering, I would say that it applies there because fatty meat seeps into things, but not to a meal offering. So both were needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: why does the תורה teach the absorption rule twice, once for חטאת and once for מנחה? It shows that each one has its own special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה is soft, so it soaks in easily. A חטאת is fatty meat, so it seeps into whatever it touches. Since each has a reason the other lacks, we could not learn one from the other, and the תורה had to write both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed: both cases had to be written
Soft (the flour of a מנחה)
It is absorbed or soaks in
Fatty
Seeps in or penetrates

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule. The גמרא is only explaining why the תורה wrote the same rule in two places.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write it by a sin offering,
phrases.notes: This is the rule from Step 9, that whatever touches it becomes holy. See ויקרא 6:20 for חטאת and ויקרא 6:11 for מנחה.

phrases.english: and it was necessary to write it by a meal offering.
For if the Merciful One had written it only by a meal offering,
I would say that it applies because it is soft and soaks in,
but for a sin offering I would say it does not.
And if the Merciful One had written it only by a sin offering,
I would say that it applies because the meat is fatty and seeps in,
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has קדיר in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is קריר, meaning it seeps in.

phrases.english: but for a meal offering I would say it does not.
So both were needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב בְּחַטָּאת, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב בְּמִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the absorption rule from Step 9 had to be written in two places
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has a unique reason, so neither can be learned from the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One source would have been enough to teach the absorption rule
steps.terutzMaskana: Soft flour and fatty meat each absorb for a different reason, so both had to be written

steps.title: What we learn from ״חטאת״: חולין, daytime, and the right hand
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: from ״חטאת״ we learn that every קרבן in the list comes only from חולין, is offered by day, and is done with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: From ״sin offering″: just as a sin offering comes only from non-holy property, by day, and with the right hand, so too every offering in the list comes only from non-holy property, by day, and with the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to its list of קרבנות and now learns three rules from the word ״חטאת״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three features are known about a חטאת: it is paid for with חולין, it is offered by day, and the כהן does the עבודה with his right hand. The ברייתא extends all three to every קרבן in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy property
In the daytime
His right hand (of the כהן)

phrases.english: "Sin offering":
just as a sin offering is brought only
from non-holy property,
and by day, and with his right hand,
so too all of them are brought only
from non-holy property,
and by day, and with his right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה חַטָּאת אֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the ברייתא's list of what each קרבן in the פסוק teaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every קרבן in the list comes only from חולין, is offered by day, and is done with the right hand

steps.title: Where do we learn the חולין rule for a חטאת itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a חטאת itself must come from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the sin offering itself, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא used the חטאת as the model. Now the גמרא asks how we know the rule for the חטאת in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn from a model if the model's own rule is proven. So the גמרא wants the source that a חטאת must come from חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And for the sin offering itself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the model case used in Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a חטאת must come from חולין

steps.title: רב חסדא: ״אשר לו״ means from his own, not from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from ״אשר לו״ that the פר החטאת must come from the owner's own property, not from מעשר money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: the פסוק says, "And אהרן shall offer the bull of the sin offering which is his." "His" means from his own property, and not from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question with a פסוק about the חטאת of יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word ״לו″ ("his″) shows that the animal must be truly his own. מעשר שני money is not fully his own because it is holy, so a חטאת cannot be bought with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull of the sin offering
From his own property
Second tithe; its money is holy and must be spent in ירושלים

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
as the verse says:
"And Aaron shall offer the bull of the sin offering
which is his":
"his" means from his own,
and not from tithe money.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From ״אשר לו״: the חטאת must come from the owner's own property, not from מעשר

steps.title: But the daytime rule already comes from ״ביום צותו״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why learn the daytime rule from חטאת, when it is already learned from ״ביום צותו״?
steps.simpleTranslation: By day? That is learned from "on the day He commanded"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one part of Step 11: the daytime rule seems to have its own separate source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״ביום צותו״ already teach that all קרבנות are offered by day. So why does the ברייתא need to learn it from חטאת? That makes this part of the ברייתא look unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from
On the day He commanded: the source that קרבנות are offered by day

phrases.english: By day?
That is learned from "on the day He commanded"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא in Step 11 and questions the daytime rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's learning of the daytime rule from חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule that already has its own פסוק does not need to be learned again from חטאת

steps.title: The ברייתא mentioned the daytime rule only along with the others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא listed the daytime rule for no special reason, just along with the other rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge: the daytime rule really comes from ״ביום צותו״, and the ברייתא just included it in its list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits that the daytime rule is not really learned from ״חטאת״. It comes from ״ביום צותו״, and the ברייתא added ״by day״ only because it fit with the other features of a חטאת. The next step asks the same question about the right-hand rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He mentioned it for nothing, just along with the others

steps.whatToRemember: The daytime rule really comes from ״ביום צותו״. The ברייתא listed it from ״חטאת״ only along with the other features of a חטאת.

phrases.english: He mentioned it for nothing.
phrases.notes: Literally, "he took it for nothing": the ברייתא listed it just because it fit with the other rules, not as a new teaching.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes that the item is not a real teaching here and was only listed along with the others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was teaching the daytime rule as a new teaching from חטאת
steps.terutzMaskana: The daytime rule comes from ״ביום צותו״, and the ברייתא listed it only alongside the other rules

steps.title: Why learn the right-hand rule from חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the rule that the עבודה is done with the right hand is already known from רבה בר בר חנה in the name of ריש לקיש, so why learn it from חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said we learn from חטאת that the service is done 'with his right hand.' But we already know that from רבה בר בר חנה! He said in the name of ריש לקיש: any place the תורה says 'finger' or 'כהונה,' it means only the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question as before, this time about the right-hand rule. It says this rule already has its own source, so the ברייתא does not need חטאת for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the גמרא asked this about the daytime rule. Now it asks it about the right-hand rule. ריש לקיש has a general rule: wherever the תורה mentions 'finger' or 'כהונה,' only the right hand counts. So why would the ברייתא need to learn it from חטאת?

keyTerms.meaning: Right hand
Finger; when the תורה mentions it, the service is done with the right hand
Priesthood; a service done by a כהן
It comes out from; it is learned from

phrases.english: With his right hand:
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא's rule from step 11, which said the right-hand rule comes from חטאת.

phrases.english: This is learned from רבה בר בר חנה!

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: For רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of ריש לקיש:
Any place where it says 'finger' or 'priesthood,'
it means only the right hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 14's challenge, now applied to the right-hand rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the right-hand rule is learned from חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule already has a separate, general source (ריש לקיש's rule about 'finger' and 'כהונה'), so learning it from חטאת seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The ברייתא just mentioned it along with the others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא mentioned the right-hand rule for no special reason, as part of its list.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא just mentioned it for no special reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave in step 15. The ברייתא did not really need חטאת for the right-hand rule; it just listed it with the other rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits the right-hand rule really comes from ריש לקיש. The ברייתא included it only because it was listing the rules that apply to חטאת. The ברייתא's real new teaching from חטאת is the חולין rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For nothing; without a special reason
He took it; he mentioned it
He mentioned it for no special reason, just along with the rest

steps.whatToRemember: From חטאת the ברייתא really needs only the חולין rule. The daytime and right-hand rules have their own sources and were listed just along with it.

phrases.english: He mentioned it for no special reason.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The ברייתא's wording is not a real derivation, just a list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא was learning the right-hand rule from חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from ריש לקיש. The ברייתא only mentioned it along with the other rules.

steps.title: From אשם: the bones are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: just as the bones of an אשם are permitted, so too the bones of every קרבן in the list are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the word 'אשם' we learn: just as the bones of an אשם are permitted, so too the bones of all these קרבנות are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא. Now it gives the rule learned from the next word in the פסוק, אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק's list teaches a rule for all the קרבנות in it. From אשם we learn that its bones have no קדושה and may be used. The same is true for every קרבן in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Its bones
Permitted for use
Just as ... so too; a comparison formula

phrases.english: 'Guilt offering':
Just as the bones of a guilt offering are permitted,
so too the bones of all of them are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about חטאת, the גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bones of every קרבן in the list are permitted for use, like the bones of an אשם.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא do with ״וזבחת פסח״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to ask: רבי עקיבא learns the חולין rule from the ברייתא's פסוק, so what does he learn from ״וזבחת פסח״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, this פסוק 'And you shall sacrifice the פסח'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. The question will finish in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה learns from ״וזבחת פסח״ that required קרבנות come only from חולין. רבי עקיבא learns that rule from the ברייתא's פסוק instead. So the גמרא wants to know what he uses ״וזבחת פסח״ for.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall sacrifice
The קרבן פסח
This

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא:
this פסוק, 'And you shall sacrifice the Paschal offering'
phrases.notes: דברים 16:2. The question finishes in the next line of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's list to a new question about how רבי עקיבא uses the משנה's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי עקיבא learns from ״וזבחת פסח״, since he does not need it for the חולין rule.
